A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SensorLLM research. All 25 pages of v3 and 26 pages of v4, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original sensor-description evaluations, human ratings, HAR experiments on five datasets, ablations, and cross-dataset transfer results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark evaluations, ablations, human assessments, and appendix examples.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the frozen Chronos and LLaMA backbones, MLP alignment module, channel-boundary tokens, generation objective, and HAR classifier. The rewritten data-generation description documents the same procedure.

E1.justification: Both use USC-HAD, UCI-HAR, PAMAP2, MHealth, and CAPTURE-24 for the same description and recognition tasks, plus the same cross-dataset transfer scenarios. Removing the SensorQA name does not remove its underlying data or tasks.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains GPT-4o, and Table 2 retains the same eleven baselines, including Attend, Chronos+MLP, and GPT4TS. Newly discussed IMUGPT and ZARA are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The subject splits, downsampling, window sizes, training budgets, metrics, and evaluation sample sizes remain unchanged. Training/testing counts in v3 Table 12 are retained in v4 Table 7.

E4.justification: Section 5 retains the alignment, prompt, MLP-depth, model-size, special-token, and cross-dataset analyses. Appendix Tables 13–14 retain the same qualitative examples.

E5.justification: Both report HAR means and standard deviations over five random repetitions and retain the same uncertainty reporting in ablation and transfer tables. No statistical testing or uncertainty-estimation procedure is added.

E6.justification: All fourteen matched table bodies and the plotted results retain their values and outputs. Section 4.3 newly spells out performance margins already represented in the unchanged Table 2.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11 retain the same projection, losses, normalization, Chronos quantization, and F1 definitions. No formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: v3 explicitly presents creation and release of the novel SensorQA dataset as a contribution. v4 instead emphasizes the automatic alignment approach and generation pipeline, while retaining the main HAR performance and cross-dataset generalization claims.

C2.justification: Section 7 removes v3's assertion about supporting unseen activity classes and its lack-of-comparable-baselines rationale for omitting zero-shot evaluation. v4 more clearly identifies classifier limitations and leaves alternative heads and zero-shot recognition to future work. Section 4.3 also adds a dataset-specific interpretation of Chronos embeddings.

D1.justification: The conclusion changes the stated release from code plus the SensorQA dataset to code plus a data-generation pipeline. The repository link, templates, sample counts, hardware, and settings remain documented; the PDFs do not establish that actual data access was withdrawn.

R1.justification: v4 expands the existing HAR literature discussion with IMUGPT and ZARA and adds Tan et al.'s critique of LLM usefulness to the introduction. Xia and Ji were already discussed in v3's appendix. Other reference changes largely update metadata or consolidate duplicate entries.

P1.justification: Rewriting spans the title, abstract, introduction, contribution list, Section 3.1, result narratives, conclusion, and classifier limitations. The HAR literature discussion moves into Section 2, and the separate SensorQA appendix subsection is consolidated into A.2, substantially revising the narrative presentation.

P2.justification: The four figures retain their content, while displays are repositioned through repagination. The sample-count table moves from Table 12 to Table 7, subsequent appendix tables are renumbered, and the class-distribution table occupies a separate page. No substantive figure or table redesign occurs.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves scientific clarity through more candid classifier and zero-shot limitations, broader relevant research positioning, and explicit table-supported comparisons. The dataset contribution is reframed around its generation pipeline while technical documentation remains available. The empirical evidence is unchanged, so the improvement is limited to framing, interpretation, and presentation.
